"My Slime Garden" is an unusual dual-mode game that borrows mechanics not dissimilar to Pokemon or Slime Rancher with a somewhat mediocre 3D rendered 2D top down shooter mode... I guess the first thing to say is that this is very early access and also that it looks like it's designed for console appliances, rather than PC. That alone may be enough to deter gamers. What do you do in the game? There's a lot to do here... the slime breeding/raising game feels like a full tycoon game for console gamers to enjoy, and a lot of welcome depth there. It's just a shame the production values are so poor and the top down/iso shooter component is contentless, dead and busted before the game is even complete. The graphics aren't great... a blend of low poly/minimalist basic assets and a few garbage looking 2D retro pixelcrap images for various components in the rancher mode. Bad graphics like this will understandably be a turn off for a lot of gamers, and it's a big contributor to the failure of the game to attract gamers despite having no up-front cost. Gaming is a primarily visual medium, and if developers want to succeed, they must understand that it's not an area for compromise. You deserve better than compromises. The developer chose not to do the job of a real game developer and create meaningful bespoke levels, narrative based gameplay progression and so on. Instead, they decided that "Procgen IS content!" and lazily tried to use procgen algorithms to create infinite, samey, repetitive, soulless levels, because that's a lot less work. As a result of this poor decision, the game gets tired and repetitive almost immediately. Developers must learn that procgen is a terrible substitute for creating real content. It should not be used as "ez-mode" for content creation, as the developer tried to do here. Not every "free" game really is. There's often MTX, or content locked behind DLC, or donations being requested, or any other number of things that could mislead gamers, but in this case I'm glad to say this really does appear to be a fully free game. Nothing demonstrates a developers belief in themselves and their work than giving it away without any remuneration. This is a service to themselves, and the gaming industry, and should be applauded. Of course, just because something is free, doesn't necessarily mean it's valuable. Even though this is "free", it failed to appeal to the 120 million+ gamers on Steam. SteamDB showed the game peaked at just a dozen or so concurrent players, and now there's basically nobody playing it. Even though it's free. This is a dismal public reception, but it's easy to see why gamers rejected it. Bearing in mind that free games don't add +1 to your game collector count, should you bother adding this to your library and downloading it? This is a "maybe" experience... if you have a lot of free time on your hands and nothing else to do, why not? But for the purposes of a review, this isn't something I can say everyone must try. It's not quite there. Valve doesn't give us a "maybe" option in reviews, but if they did, that's what I'd choose for this.

Very very addicting gameplay and adorable slime petting. There's a LOT of features I honestly did not expect to see in a free game like this! The co-op, the fishing, the desktop mode, there's a crazy variety of things to do. That said, UI could be a little better, the islands could use some more variation and the gameplay could some polishing overall, but I see a lot of potential!

Cool game, will write a longer review at some point. Only complaints I've got are that the expeditions are super repetitive after a while (not enough variety) and there's only one (1) parkour map (and it's solved only one way, so it becomes mindless after doing it once.)

You ever play Sonic Adventure 2 and think "wow, what if this little Chao Garden thing was a whole game?" I mean I'm sure everyone thought this, right? Well now you don't have to think it, because there's this little charming roguelike beat 'em up mixed with adorable little slime dudes and dudettes and you can sit in a garden and feed them and pet them and then make them go and do a crime. The dev is also quite active in updating and adding new content as it is all done as a passion project (did I mention the price tag of nothing, nada, zilch, zero, absolutely no wallet drain whatsoever???) so you can just go hit play game now and thank me later when your slime is powerful enough to destroy the world but it spares you because you fed it some apples and gave it headpats.

The game dev happened to call me and my bf over at Too Many Games this weekend to show us this game, and I am SO GLAD he did! This game is so cute and so much fun, and has so many different mechanics and game modes, plus on top of that being entirely free?! I was initially a little worried I wouldn't get very far since I'm not great at roguelikes, but there's multiple ways of scaling difficulty, so I can see both beginners and experts being able to find it fun yet challenging. I was hooked immediately, and I highly recommend at least giving it a try, it's a wonderful game with SO much passion and talent behind it!
